title: A geometrically irreducible scheme surjects onto the Hilbert scheme
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a curve over $k$ [def-pc-curve] that is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and geometrically integral [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] [def-pc-integral-scheme], let $d\geq0$, and let $H$ be a $k$-scheme representing [def-pc-representable-functor] the functor $\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{X/k}$ [def-pc-hilb-functor]. Then there exist a $k$-scheme $Y$, a proper morphism $q:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, and a morphism $\pi:Y\to H$ such that $Y$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], $\pi$ is surjective, and $\pi$ followed by $H\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ equals $q$.

source.place: Tag 0B9I (proposition-hilb-d), proof of (1): iterated addition from X^d to Hilb^d; X^d is geometrically irreducible by Varieties, Lemma 038F

proof.text: *Setup.* Let $p:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure morphism. Since $X$ is geometrically integral, every base change $X_{k'}$ ($k'/k$ a field extension) is integral, hence irreducible by [lem-pc-integral-scheme-irreducible]; so $X$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. The morphism $p$ is separated, $X$ being a curve, hence a variety [def-pc-curve], and proper by hypothesis. Applying [lem-sc-curve-base-change-relative-dimension-one] with $T=\operatorname{Spec}k$ (so $X_T=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k\cong X$ over $k$) shows that $p$ is smooth of relative dimension $1$. Thus $X$ is a geometrically irreducible smooth proper curve over $k$, and by [thm-pc-hilb-curves] (1) the functor $\operatorname{Hilb}^e_{X/k}$ [def-pc-hilb-functor] is representable for every $e\geq0$. For $e\neq d$ choose a $k$-scheme $H_e$ representing $\operatorname{Hilb}^e_{X/k}$ [def-pc-representable-functor], and put $H_d:=H$; write $h_e:H_e\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ for the structure morphisms.

source.place: Tag 0B9I (proposition-hilb-d), proof, first sentence (representability by 0B9A and Varieties 0A26) and 'Starting with ... the morphisms of Lemma 0B9G'

proof.text: *The addition morphisms are surjective.* By the previous step $p$ is separated and smooth of relative dimension $1$ and all $\operatorname{Hilb}^e_{X/k}$ are representable, so [lem-pc-hilb-addition] (with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, applied to the representing schemes $H_e$, $H_{e+1}$) gives for every $e\geq0$ a morphism $a_e:H_e\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}X\to H_{e+1}$ which is finite locally free of degree $e+1$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. It is a morphism over $k$: the lemma defines it on $T$-valued points for $k$-schemes $T$ (a pair $(Z,x)$ goes to $Z+x$), i.e. as a transformation of functors on $(\mathit{Sch}/k)$, which by the Yoneda lemma is a morphism of $k$-schemes, $h_{e+1}\circ a_e=h_e\circ\mathrm{pr}_1$. Each $a_e$ is surjective: for $s\in H_{e+1}$ the fibre $F_s=(H_e\times_kX)\times_{H_{e+1}}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ has $\dim_{\kappa(s)}\Gamma(F_s,\mathcal O_{F_s})=e+1\geq1$ by [def-pc-finite-locally-free], so $F_s$ is not empty; for a point $z\in F_s$, its image $y$ in $H_e\times_kX$ satisfies $a_e(y)=s$, because the fibre square commutes and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to H_{e+1}$ has image $\{s\}$.

source.place: Tag 0B9I (proposition-hilb-d), proof of (1): 'Starting with ..., the morphisms of Lemma 0B9G (lemma-universal-object), and induction we find a morphism X^d -> Hilb^d ... which is finite locally free of degree d!'; Tag 0B9G for the degree

proof.text: *Inductive claim and base.* We prove by induction on $e\geq0$: (P$_e$) there are a $k$-scheme $Y_e$ with proper structure morphism $q_e:Y_e\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], geometrically irreducible over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and a surjective morphism $\pi_e:Y_e\to H_e$ [def-weil-surjective-morphism] with $h_e\circ\pi_e=q_e$. For $e=0$: by [lem-sc-hilb-zero-base] (with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$), $h_0:H_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is an isomorphism. Take $Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $q_0=\mathrm{id}$, $\pi_0=h_0^{-1}$. Then $\pi_0$ is an isomorphism, hence surjective, and $h_0\circ\pi_0=\mathrm{id}=q_0$. The identity is a closed immersion, hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. For every field extension $k'/k$ the base change $\operatorname{Spec}k\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'\cong\operatorname{Spec}k'$ [def-pc-base-change] is a single point, hence irreducible; so $Y_0$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$.

source.place: Tag 0B9G (lemma-universal-object), preceding text: 'Observe that Hilb^0_{X/S} = S and Hilb^1_{X/S} = X'; Tag 0B9I proof of (1), 'and induction'

proof.text: *Induction step: the scheme $Y_{e+1}$.* Assume (P$_e$). Put $Y_{e+1}:=Y_e\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}X$, the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] of $q_e$ and $p$, with projections $\mathrm{pr}_1,\mathrm{pr}_2$, and $q_{e+1}:=q_e\circ\mathrm{pr}_1$ (equal to $p\circ\mathrm{pr}_2$). The projection $\mathrm{pr}_1:Y_{e+1}\to Y_e$ is the base change of the proper morphism $p$ along $q_e$, hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]; so $q_{e+1}$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. Since $Y_e$ (by (P$_e$)) and $X$ (by the first step) are geometrically irreducible over $k$, $Y_{e+1}$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$ by [lem-sc-geometrically-irreducible-product].

source.place: Tag 0B9I (proposition-hilb-d), proof of (1): 'Since X is proper over k, so is X^d' and 'Since X is geometrically irreducible over k, the product X^d is irreducible (Varieties, Lemma 038F)'

proof.text: *Induction step: the morphism $\pi_{e+1}$.* Since $h_e\circ\pi_e=q_e$, the morphisms $\pi_e\circ\mathrm{pr}_1$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2$ define $\pi_e\times\mathrm{id}_X:Y_e\times_kX\to H_e\times_kX$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The square with sides $\pi_e\times\mathrm{id}_X$, $\mathrm{pr}_1:Y_e\times_kX\to Y_e$, $\mathrm{pr}_1:H_e\times_kX\to H_e$ and $\pi_e$ is cartesian: by the universal properties, a morphism $T\to Y_e\times_{H_e}(H_e\times_kX)$ is a pair $(y,(\eta,x))$ with $\pi_e y=\eta$ and $h_e\eta=p x$, i.e. a pair $(y,x)$ with $q_e y=h_e\pi_e y=px$, i.e. a morphism $T\to Y_e\times_kX$. Hence $\pi_e\times\mathrm{id}_X$ is the base change of the surjective $\pi_e$ along $H_e\times_kX\to H_e$, and is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Put $\pi_{e+1}:=a_e\circ(\pi_e\times\mathrm{id}_X):Y_{e+1}\to H_{e+1}$; it is surjective as a composite of surjective maps (second step). Finally $h_{e+1}\circ\pi_{e+1}=h_e\circ\mathrm{pr}_1\circ(\pi_e\times\mathrm{id}_X)=h_e\circ\pi_e\circ\mathrm{pr}_1=q_e\circ\mathrm{pr}_1=q_{e+1}$, using that $a_e$ is over $k$ (second step). This proves (P$_{e+1}$). On points, $\pi_{e+1}(y,x)=\pi_e(y)+x$, so for $e\geq1$, $Y_e=X^e$ and $\pi_e$ is $(x_1,\dots,x_e)\mapsto x_1+\cdots+x_e$, the morphism of the source.

source.place: Tag 0B9I (proposition-hilb-d), proof of (1): 'we find a morphism X^d -> Hilb^d, (x_1,...,x_d) -> x_1+...+x_d, which is finite locally free of degree d!' (here only surjectivity is kept, obtained from the degrees e+1 >= 1 of the factors)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* (P$_d$) gives $Y:=Y_d$ (the $d$-fold fibre product $X^d=X\times_k\cdots\times_kX$ for $d\geq1$, $\operatorname{Spec}k$ for $d=0$), the proper morphism $q:=q_d:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, with $Y$ geometrically irreducible over $k$, and the surjective $\pi:=\pi_d:Y\to H_d=H$ with $h_d\circ\pi=q$, which is the statement.
